caption:
Austin homeowners have a $295 million decision on the November 3 ballot.

The City’s bond package is split into two propositions:

• Proposition A: $260 million for parks and recreation
• Proposition B: $35 million for libraries

The parks proposal includes facilities, park improvements, pools, infrastructure, trails and land acquisition. The library proposal includes $20 million for the Hampton Branch renovation and expansion in Oak Hill and $15 million for a new Colony Park branch.

What about property taxes? City estimates indicate that a homeowner with an average-valued $495,000 home would pay approximately $40 more per year if the full package passes and the debt is issued. Individual impact would depend on taxable value, exemptions and when the bonds are sold.

The two propositions are voted on separately. Approval would authorize the City to issue debt for the listed capital projects; it would not mean all $295 million is spent immediately.

This is an information post, not an endorsement. Review the official ballot language before voting.

Sources: KUT, October 15, 2026; City of Austin bond materials.
